title: Lockstep run under left-block embedding
statement: Let $k,l\in\mathbb N$, let $M$ have $k$ work tapes and states in $S$, and let $M'$ have $k+l$ work tapes and states in $S'$, both over Boolean symbols. Suppose $f:S\to S'$ and, for every state $q$, input symbol (possibly absent), and tuple of symbols on the $k+l$ work tapes, the transition of $M'$ at state $f(q)$ equals the left-block extension along $f$ of the transition of $M$ at $q$, using the first $k$ tape symbols. Then for every configuration $c$ of $M$ on Boolean input $x$, every choice of contents and head positions for the last $l$ tapes, and every $t\in\mathbb N$, running $M'$ for $t$ steps from the embedded configuration equals the embedding of the configuration reached by running $M$ for $t$ steps from $c$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ has $k$ Boolean work tapes and state type $S$
$M'$ has $k+l$ Boolean work tapes and state type $S'$
the transition compatibility condition holds for all $q$, input symbols, and work-symbol tuples
$c$ is a configuration of $M$ on Boolean input $x$
contents and head positions for the last $l$ tapes are arbitrary
replaced:
Let $M$ be a machine with $k$ work tapes and $M'$ a machine with $k + l$ work
tapes, both over the Boolean alphabet, and let $f$ be a map from the states
of $M$ to the states of $M'$ such that on every renamed state, for all
scanned symbols, the transition of $M'$ is the left-block extension along $f$
of the corresponding transition of $M$ read off the first $k$ tapes.  Then
for every configuration $c$ of $M$ on input $x$, all inactive contents and
head positions for the last $l$ tapes, and every number of steps $t$, running
$M'$ for $t$ steps from the left-block embedding of $c$ equals the left-block
embedding of the run of $M$ for $t$ steps from $c$.
